s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute bilateral visual disturbance with transient visual obscuration and tinnitus, associated with optic disc edema and posterior fossa abnormalities
salient_findings: Bilateral blurry vision with transient visual obscurations
key_facts: Optic disc edema worse in the right eye
Disc hemorrhages and exudates in the right eye
Multiple cysts in the posterior fossa
Large cyst at the level of the fourth ventricle

raw.syndrome_frame: Subacute bilateral visual disturbance with transient visual obscuration and tinnitus, associated with optic disc edema and posterior fossa abnormalities
salient_findings: Bilateral blurry vision with transient visual obscurations
key_facts: Optic disc edema worse in the right eye
Disc hemorrhages and exudates in the right eye
Multiple cysts in the posterior fossa
Large cyst at the level of the fourth ventricle

differentials: Intracranial Hypertension due to Venous Outflow Obstruction
Paget Disease of the Bone with Neurological Involvement
Fibrous Dysplasia with Optic Nerve Compression
per_call: Intracranial Hypertension due to Venous Outflow Obstruction
Paget Disease of the Bone with Neurological Involvement
Fibrous Dysplasia with Optic Nerve Compression

shortlist.label: Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral optic disc edema and transient visual obscurations are classic symptoms

shortlist.label: Pseudotumor Cerebri
shortlist.why_kept: Similar symptoms to idiopathic intracranial hypertension, with possible connection to obstructive hydrocephalus

shortlist.label: Arachnoid Cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Posterior fossa cysts could be causing obstructive hydrocephalus and subsequent visual symptoms

shortlist.label: Dandy-Walker Malformation
shortlist.why_kept: Congenital condition that could explain posterior fossa abnormalities and hydrocephalus

shortlist.label: Craniopharyngioma
shortlist.why_kept: Tumor in the posterior fossa could be causing obstructive hydrocephalus and visual disturbances

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of bilateral blurry vision, transient visual obscurations, and optic disc edema are consistent with increased intracranial pressure, and the presence of obstructive hydrocephalus due to the cysts could be a contributing factor, but the normal CSF analysis and the specific characteristics of the optic disc edema and symptoms point more directly to idiopathic intracranial hypertension.

rejected.label: Pseudotumor Cerebri
rejected.why: Pseudotumor cerebri is another term for idiopathic intracranial hypertension, so it's essentially the same condition, not a distinct alternative.

rejected.label: Arachnoid Cyst
rejected.why: While the patient has arachnoid cysts, they are not the primary cause of the symptoms; the cysts are more likely contributing to the obstructive hydrocephalus, which in turn could be related to the increased intracranial pressure.

rejected.label: Dandy-Walker Malformation
rejected.why: This condition typically presents in infancy with symptoms of hydrocephalus and is characterized by a specific set of anatomical malformations, which do not match the patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Craniopharyngioma
rejected.why: This is a type of brain tumor that could cause increased intracranial pressure and visual disturbances, but the description provided does not specifically indicate a tumor mass affecting the optic nerves or chiasm, and the presence of cysts in the posterior fossa does not align with the typical location of craniopharyngiomas.
